events.title: Safeguarding LLMs via Model-Agnostic Latent Safety Signals from Dark Knowledge
events.summary: A research paper on arXiv proposes a model-agnostic way to improve LLM safety at decoding time using latent signals, aimed at avoiding the usual trade-off between blocking attacks and over-refusing benign requests, and not depending on a specific model architecture.
events.why_it_matters: For teams deploying LLMs, the method addresses two practical limits of current decoding-stage defences: safety tightening that degrades helpfulness on benign queries, and dependence on internal hidden states that ties defences to particular architectures. A model-agnostic approach could be applied across different models rather than only one family. The record gives no real-world deployment or exploitation details, so its practical impact is unproven.

events.title: Provable Authority: A Protocol for Verifiable Authority Resolution and Control Across Human, Organizational, and Agentic Transactions
events.summary: An arXiv paper proposes a protocol for compact, independently verifiable evidence of an actor's current organisational authority to execute a specific transaction, spanning human, organisational, and AI-agent dealings. It argues today's payment authentication cannot prove the presenter was actually authorised, a gap the paper says becomes urgent with autonomous purchasing agents.
events.why_it_matters: If agentic commerce grows, relying parties such as payment rails and marketplaces may need cryptographic proof that an agent acted within its delegated budget and approval limits, not just that a signature is valid. The paper outlines a design approach defenders and payment-system builders could evaluate, though it is untested research rather than an exploited flaw.

events.title: Amazon CloudWatch EKS Container Insights now offers built-in monitoring for open source Kubernetes tools
events.summary: Amazon CloudWatch Container Insights for EKS now includes built-in monitoring for popular open source Kubernetes tools such as Karpenter, KEDA, vLLM, KServe, Ray and Knative, with automatic activation when OTel Container Insights is enabled. The feature provides prebuilt dashboards, including metrics for AI inference workloads and autoscaling behaviour.
events.why_it_matters: Teams running Kubernetes on AWS can observe their autoscaling and AI inference stacks without operating their own Prometheus or Grafana, with metrics like time to first token and KV cache usage per model server. Better visibility into failing scalers and scale-loop timing may help detect operational issues earlier.

events.title: Gootloader WordPress Sites: FBI Warns of Ransomware
events.summary: The FBI has issued a FLASH notice describing Gootloader's use of compromised WordPress sites as a distribution network that ultimately provides access for ransomware operators. As of October, the campaign involved over 1,000 infected WordPress sites and 216 administrator-controlled domains, and the FBI links it to more than $28 million in ransomware payments.
events.why_it_matters: The scale of compromised WordPress sites and the reported $28 million in ransomware payments make this a broadly relevant initial-access threat for any organisation running WordPress or receiving SEO-driven downloads. The FBI FLASH notice is designed to help defenders detect and block the infrastructure, so IOCs from it are worth acting on.
